operations.summary: Agent definitions: kind, identity, owner, tier ceiling, tools, scope, limits, triggers
One agent definition
Sessions you may see, newest first: limits, budget used, breaker, run, parent, expiry; state is live, closed or expired
One session: with input (what an in-cluster run was asked) and outcome (how it ended) once it has them
A finished in-cluster run's answer (results.py), kept 30 days: status, final_text, turns, tool_calls [{tool, ok, rule}], reason; 404 when there is none or it expired
A run tree: every session of the task, with parent links and totals
Evidence records you may see, newest first; the cursor is seq
One evidence record with its hash
The whole chain checked from genesis: ok, count, head, the first bad seq
Records you may see, counted by rule, tool, agent, app or decision (`by`), with the same filters as the list
The policy in force: the deny rules in evaluation order (id, name, CEL expression, message, hint, pack), the tool registry with tiers, the packs
Would this be allowed? A dry run of the real policy for an agent, a tool and its args (JSON) on a fresh session: the decision and each rule's verdict in order. Records nothing
PR receipts: what Clearance's agents opened on a repo (and PR), the commit, the paths
The agent-gate verdicts recorded for a PR (provenance.verify)
Pending human requests: a person's, those they may answer; a notifier's, every pending one (with owner and group), created since `since`

The events the trigger bridge received, newest first, each with what it did per agent (launched, deduped, braked, refused): the history a trigger dry run, an agent's trigger statistics and an app's run marks read. Kept 30 days; the cursor is received_at

The deployment gate's changes (gate.py), newest first: tier and why, state (holding, cleared, denied, expired, superseded), the requirement and the approvals so far, what the grant binds to. A person sees their apps' changes and the ones their groups may clear; the cursor is updated_at
Changes counted by state, tier, app, env or cleared_by (the C1 stats: holding, cleared by policy and by people, denied)
One change: the objects and paths it touches, every reason for its tier, the requirement, the approvals, the checks as last reported
The deployment gate's baseline policy: the tier table, the people each tier needs, the outside groups, the TTL. A repo's clearance.yaml can only tighten it
The deployment's runtime catalog (runtimes.py): the agent images a definition may run (kind runtime) or a code agent may build FROM (kind base), each pinned by digest, with its framework and status
This contract
